To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MRAS based speed estimation techniques can be used during severe voltage dips for the independent control and to achieve maximum efficiency of the wind turbine.
the performance of MRAS speed estimator depends on the voltage level, the rotor resistance and the rotor flux.
MRAS speed estimator with rotor flux as reference is found to be more accurate and reliable during voltage dips.
In summary, our research is concerned with
(1) Performance evaluation of different MRAS speed estimator under voltage dips.
the performance evaluation of MRAS based rotor speed estimators for doubly fed wind energy conversion systems under voltage dips.
the performance of speed estimators during voltage dip and also the effect of resistance on speed estimation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of MRAS based estimator is better than other estimators during voltage dip conditions.
the performance of the proposed MRAS based speed estimator during grid voltage dips is better than other MRAS based speed estimation techniques.

the performance of MRAS speed estimator is affected by voltage dips and the performance is better for MRAS speed estimator based on stator current and stator flux linkage as compared to other speed estimators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the performance of MRAS based rotor speed estimators during voltage dip is not satisfactory.
the speed estimation performance is not much affected under voltage dips and resistance variations.
the MRAS speed estimation techniques have been studied under normal operating condition and during grid voltage dips up to the extent as per the grid codes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of speed estimators is affected by the voltage dips and the resistance variation.

the performance of all the MRAs based estimators degrades during voltage dips, and the speed estimation accuracy of the MRAS based estimator with the stator flux and rotor flux as reference signals is better as compared to the other MRAS based estimations techniques.
the performance of all MRAS speed estimator deteriorates during voltage dips and the performance of resistance variation method based speed estimator deteriorates further.
